properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The sharpest technical problem inside `dec:idea-does-reflow2-ship-design-principles-to-every-project`, and the one that decides whether shipping is even possible.

THE PROBLEM, read straight off dev_storyflow's own text. Every one of the seven principles is a universal idea wearing storyflow's clothes:

  #2 "no silent fallbacks" — the IDEA is universal (a failure must never report success). The STATEMENT names `try/except: pass`, `console.error`, toast UI. A beamline control system has the same failure and none of those words.
  #4 "verify your own claims" — universal. The statement names `npm run check`, foreground cargo, Playwright on a real surface.
  #5 "real-path tests" — universal. "Unit-green ≠ live-green" survives translation; "the path the UI actually calls" does not.
  #7 "modular, no monoliths" — the modularity half travels; the Python DI / `typing.Protocol` / flat-hierarchy half is a language ruling and travels nowhere.
  #3 "done = end-to-end + lens-exposed" — travels as "built is not delivered"; "lens-exposed" is storyflow vocabulary.
  #1 and #6 travel almost verbatim, which is itself informative: they are the two most abstract.

⇒ SHIPPING THE PROSE AS-IS WOULD PUT A JAVASCRIPT TOAST IN A BEAMLINE'S DESIGN GRAPH. And reflow2's operating context is explicitly not one domain — greenfield and brownfield, several orgs, currently a ~10-year-old bluesky stack at a synchrotron. A principle that arrives wearing the wrong clothes gets waived for the clothes, and the idea goes with them.

THE SHAPES, none chosen:
(A) CORE ONLY. Ship the domain-free statement; each project writes its own instantiation if it wants one. Cheapest and most portable. COST: the abstract version is the forgettable version — "fail loudly" is a poster, whereas "no `try/except: pass`" is a thing you can be caught doing. The teeth are in the clothes.
(B) CORE + WORKED EXAMPLES, marked as examples. The statement is domain-free; illustrations are labelled as one domain's instantiation, not as the rule. Keeps the teeth without asserting them elsewhere. COST: longer nodes, and `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` already says this design writes too much into single fields.
(C) CORE + A PROJECT-LOCAL INSTANTIATION SLOT. The shipped rule is the core; the project fills in what it looks like HERE, and the filling-in is the act of adopting it. Turns adoption into something visible and checkable rather than a silent inheritance. COST: new vocabulary, and a slot nobody fills is the declared-field-nobody-writes-to trap `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` names explicitly.
(D) DOMAIN PACKS. A software pack, an instrument-control pack, and so on. COST: reflow2 would be asserting what a domain is, and it has no basis for that.

⭐ AN OBSERVATION WORTH CARRYING WHICHEVER WAY THIS GOES: the two that travel verbatim (#1 root-cause-first, #6 no silent caps) are the two reflow2 has ALREADY adopted for itself, independently. That is weak evidence that portability and abstraction are the same axis here — and that the right test for "should this ship" may simply be "does it survive being stated without naming a language, a framework, or a tool?"
properties.name: OPEN — a shipped principle has a universal CORE and local CLOTHES; does reflow2 ship only the core, and how does a project put its own clothes on it?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. Every one of the seven is a universal idea in local clothes, and the clothes are where the teeth are — "fail loudly" is a poster, "no try/except: pass" is something you can be caught doing. Shipping the prose unchanged would put JavaScript toasts in a beamline's design graph; shipping only the abstraction may ship something too weak to bite. Not resolved.
